title: DAX Basics: Measures, Filter Context and CALCULATE

header.html: Create single aggregation measures; Use the CALCULATE function; Create a measure by using quick measures; Create calculated tables or columns
the official PL-300 study guide (skills measured as of April 20, 2026)

html:
1Measures and aggregation functions

A measure is a DAX formula that is calculated at query time, once for every cell of a visual, using the filters that apply to that cell.

Function What it returns
SUM The total of the numbers in a column
AVERAGE The mean of the numbers in a column
COUNT How many numbers or dates a column holds (COUNTA counts any non-blank value)
COUNTROWS How many rows a table has
DISTINCTCOUNT How many different values a column holds
MIN and MAX The smallest and the largest value
DIVIDE A division that returns blank, or an alternate result you give, instead of an error when the divisor is zero
SUMX, AVERAGEX, MAXX Iterators: evaluate an expression for each row of a table, then aggregate the results

An implicit measure appears when you drag a numeric column into a visual and Power BI aggregates it with the default summarization. An explicit measure is a measure you write in DAX. Prefer explicit measures: other measures can reuse them, results stay consistent, and calculation groups work only with them. The model setting Discourage implicit measures enforces this.

Total Sales = SUM ( Sales[Amount] )

Customers = DISTINCTCOUNT ( Sales[CustomerKey] )

Revenue = SUMX ( Sales, Sales[Quantity] * Sales[UnitPrice] )

Margin Percent = DIVIDE ( SUM ( Sales[Profit] ), [Total Sales] )

Use SUMX when the value needs a calculation on each row first. SUM of Quantity times SUM of UnitPrice gives a different, wrong answer.

Exam tip

. Use DIVIDE instead of the slash operator to avoid divide-by-zero errors. COUNT counts values in a column, COUNTROWS counts table rows, DISTINCTCOUNT counts unique values.

Exam tip

. A function ending in X is an iterator. It calculates row by row and then aggregates, so use it when the formula combines several columns of one row.

2Filter context and row context

Filter context decides which rows are visible; row context points at one row inside them.

Context What it is Where it exists
Filter context The set of filters in force while a measure is evaluated; it limits the rows each table exposes Every cell of a visual: its rows and columns, slicers, report filters, relationships and CALCULATE
Row context The current row of one table, so a formula can read that row's columns Calculated columns and the X iterator functions

A measure such as SUM(Sales[Amount]) has no current row. It adds up whatever rows survive the filter context, so each cell of a matrix gets its own answer. Filters on a dimension pass through relationships from the one side to the many side (see Module 5).

Row context does not filter other tables. When CALCULATE runs inside a row context, it turns the current row into filters. This is called context transition. It is also why a measure that you call inside a calculated column or an iterator works for each row.

Exam tip

. Calculated columns and iterators create row context; measures are evaluated in filter context. CALCULATE is the function that changes filter context, and inside a row context it converts the row into filters.

3CALCULATE and variables

CALCULATE ( expression, filter1, filter2, ... ) evaluates the expression after it changes the filter context with the filter arguments. Several filter arguments combine with AND. A filter on a different column adds to the existing filters; a filter on the same column replaces the existing one.

Filter argument or modifier Effect
Boolean filter, such as Product[Color] = "Red" Replaces any filter on that column; it can use only one column and cannot call a measure
FILTER Table filter for a condition that uses several columns or a measure
ALL Removes filters from a table or from the columns you list
REMOVEFILTERS Does the same as ALL, but only inside CALCULATE, and says what it means
ALLSELECTED Removes the filters of the visual but keeps the outer ones, such as slicers; used for percent of the selection
ALLEXCEPT Removes all filters of a table except on the columns you list
KEEPFILTERS Adds the new filter to the existing ones instead of replacing them

A variable is declared with VAR and the result is given with RETURN. It is evaluated once, where it is defined, and does not change when a later CALCULATE changes the context. Variables make a measure faster to run and easier to read.

Red Sales = CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], Product[Color] = "Red" )

Share of All Products =
VAR AllSales = CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], REMOVEFILTERS ( Product ) )
RETURN
    DIVIDE ( [Total Sales], AllSales )
Exam tip

. A Boolean filter in CALCULATE replaces the existing filter on that column. ALL and REMOVEFILTERS remove filters; ALLSELECTED keeps slicer selections, so it is the choice for a percent of what the user selected.

Exam tip

. KEEPFILTERS intersects with the existing filter instead of overwriting it. Use FILTER when a condition needs a measure or more than one column.

4Quick measures

A quick measure is a dialog on the Home tab that writes the DAX for you. You choose a calculation, drag fields into the boxes, and Power BI creates an ordinary explicit measure that you can read and edit afterwards.

Category Examples
Aggregate per category Average, minimum, maximum or weighted average per category
Filters A filtered value, or the difference from a filtered value
Time intelligence Year-to-date, quarter-to-date and month-to-date totals, year-over-year change, rolling average
Totals Running total
Mathematical operations Addition, subtraction, division, percentage difference
Text Star rating, concatenated list of values

The time intelligence quick measures cannot be used in DirectQuery. Quick measures are a good way to learn the DAX pattern, but the exam expects you to recognize the result, not to type it from memory.

Exam tip

. Quick measures create regular DAX measures, and the time intelligence category does not work with DirectQuery. Use them to build a running total or a year-over-year change without writing DAX.

5Calculated columns and calculated tables

Module 5 explains when to choose each object. Here is how they behave in DAX.

Object Context Key function
Calculated column Row context; stored in the model and computed at refresh RELATED fetches one value from the one side of a relationship
Calculated table A table expression, stored in the model CALENDARAUTO, UNION or a copy of a table

For example, a calculated column in Sales that is defined as RELATED of Product[Category] gives every sales row the category of its product. RELATED follows the relationship to the one side and returns one value. RELATEDTABLE goes the other way and returns the related rows of the many side. Both need a relationship.

Power Query is preferred when the logic can be done there. Create a column with New column on the Table tools tab, and a table with New table.

Exam tip

. RELATED returns a single value from the one side; RELATEDTABLE returns the many-side rows. Both depend on an existing relationship and a row context.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1The Sales table has Quantity and UnitPrice columns but no revenue column. A card must show total revenue. Which measure should you write?

  • ASUMX over Sales, multiplying Quantity by UnitPrice
  • BSUM of Quantity times SUM of UnitPrice across Sales
  • CCOUNTROWS of Sales times the average of UnitPrice
  • DAVERAGE of UnitPrice times the SUM of Quantity
Show the answer

Answer: A. SUMX multiplies the two columns on each row before it adds the results, whereas the other options combine totals or averages.

S2An author drags the Amount column onto a card and gets a sum. The team later wants to reuse the calculation in other measures and in a calculation group. What should the author create?

  • AA calculated column that repeats the sum on each row
  • BA calculated table that stores the sum of Amount
  • CAn explicit measure that sums the Amount column
  • DA visual calculation that sums Amount on the card
Show the answer

Answer: C. An explicit measure is named, reusable and the only kind that a calculation group can change.

S3Each Sales row must show the category of its product, which is stored in the Product table. A relationship exists between the tables. Which function should the calculated column use?

  • AThe RELATEDTABLE function on the Product table
  • BThe RELATED function on the Product Category
  • CThe USERELATIONSHIP function on Product Category
  • DThe SELECTEDVALUE function on the Product Category
Show the answer

Answer: B. RELATED follows the relationship to the one side and returns a single value for the current row.

S4A measure must total sales for all product categories even when a Category slicer is set. Region slicers must still apply. Which pattern should you use?

  • ACALCULATE with ALLSELECTED on Product Category
  • BCALCULATE with KEEPFILTERS on Product Category
  • CCALCULATE with ALL on every table in the model
  • DCALCULATE with REMOVEFILTERS on Product Category
Show the answer

Answer: D. REMOVEFILTERS on the Category column clears only that filter, while the other filters still apply.

S5A percent-of-total measure must divide by the total of the products that are shown in the visual after the slicers apply. What should the denominator use?

  • ACALCULATE with ALLSELECTED on the Product table
  • BCALCULATE with ALL on the entire Product table
  • CCALCULATE with ALLEXCEPT on the Product category
  • DCALCULATE with KEEPFILTERS on the Product table
Show the answer

Answer: A. ALLSELECTED clears the filters of the visual but keeps the slicer selections, which gives the total of what the user selected.

S6A model uses DirectQuery. An author tries to create a year-over-year change quick measure. What happens?

  • AIt works only if the Date table is marked as a date table
  • BIt is not available because the model uses DirectQuery
  • CIt works but covers only the first million rows of data
  • DIt works only when the model sits in a Premium workspace
Show the answer

Answer: B. Time intelligence quick measures cannot be used with DirectQuery.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Which function counts the unique values in a column?

Show the answer

DISTINCTCOUNT.

R2Which two kinds of formula create a row context?

Show the answer

Calculated columns and iterator (X) functions.

R3Which function avoids a divide-by-zero error?

Show the answer

DIVIDE.

R4What do VAR and RETURN do?

Show the answer

VAR stores a value once, and RETURN gives the result of the measure.

R5What does KEEPFILTERS do inside CALCULATE?

Show the answer

It keeps the existing filters and adds the new one instead of replacing them.

R6What does a quick measure produce?

Show the answer

An ordinary DAX measure that you can edit.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Aggregations SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, COUNTROWS, DISTINCTCOUNT, MIN, MAX; DIVIDE is the safe division
Iterators X functions such as SUMX work row by row, then aggregate
Explicit and implicit Explicit measures are written in DAX and reusable; Discourage implicit measures enforces them
Filter context The filters in force for a cell; row context is the current row
CALCULATE Changes the filter context; same column replaces, different column adds
Modifiers ALL and REMOVEFILTERS remove; ALLSELECTED keeps slicers; ALLEXCEPT; KEEPFILTERS intersects
Variables VAR and RETURN; evaluated once
Quick measures Home tab dialog that writes DAX; time intelligence not in DirectQuery
Calculated column Row context; RELATED (one side value) and RELATEDTABLE (many-side rows)
